claims.statement: Both Vercel projects (frontend `sangam`, backend `sangam-backend`) disable Git-triggered deployments via `git.deploymentEnabled: false` in their vercel.json and pin the function region to `bom1` (Mumbai), beside the Supabase database.

Production deploys happen only through the manually triggered (workflow_dispatch) Deploy GitHub workflow, which runs `vercel deploy --prod` for the `sangam` and `sangam-backend` projects using VERCEL_TOKEN; with no usable base ref a manual run deploys both.

The backend function `app/main.py` has maxDuration 1800 s in backend/vercel.json, and the CopilotKit proxy route in the frontend declares `maxDuration = 1800`; the two values must be kept equal because Import turns stream through the proxy for 15-20 minutes.

A Vercel cron in backend/vercel.json calls `/health` every five minutes (`*/5 * * * *`) to keep one instance warm; `/health` returns `{status: ok}` plus a counts-only `pool` object (pool_max, pool_size, pool_available, requests_waiting, requests_errors, connections_errors) once the pool exists, and is an open path that skips authentication.

The deployed backend must connect to Supabase Postgres through the session pooler on port 5432: the direct host `db.<ref>.supabase.co` is IPv6-only and hangs from containers, and the transaction pooler (6543) breaks pg_restore. The backend pool also disables prepared statements (`prepare_threshold=0`).

The backend's Postgres pool size (DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE, default 10) is sized against Supabase's 60-connection limit (3 reserved) across several instances, is shared by REST, agent tools and the checkpointer, and concurrency gates are set to max(2, pool-3) so the checkpointer is not starved; requests wait db_pool_timeout_s (10 s) for a connection and new connections get db_connect_timeout_s (5 s).

SUPABASE_URL is the auth switch: when set, the backend verifies Supabase access tokens against the project's JWKS (ES256/RS256, audience `authenticated`, issuer `<url>/auth/v1`), anonymous requests (no header) have no identity, malformed/invalid tokens are 401, and `Bearer dev` is accepted as the dev user only with DEV_AUTH; when empty every request is the seeded dev user, except that with DEV_AUTH `Bearer dev:<email>` selects a seeded @local.test user.

Supabase Storage is accessed only through backend/app/integrations/storage.py over plain httpx REST with the service-role key; it is optional (disabled when SUPABASE_URL or SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY is unset, logging once and returning None/empty) and never raises into research or promotion, so an outage leaves storage_path null instead of failing a run.

Storage uses the buckets source-archive, org-vault and staff-sources; archive keys are content-addressed (`<url-hash>/<sha256>-<name>`) at fetch and renamed to `funders/<slug>/<year>-<name>` at promotion, while vault keys are `<org_id>/<uuid>-<name>` so the org id leads for RLS; `split` rejects unknown buckets and empty/./.. segments.

Browser uploads to the Doc Vault go directly to Supabase Storage through a backend-minted signed upload URL (valid 2 hours) because Vercel Functions cap request bodies at a few MB; signed download URLs default to 10 minutes, archive uploads over 50 MB are refused client-side, and a duplicate upload (reported by Supabase as HTTP 400 with statusCode 409) counts as success.

`app/core/egress.py` provides `guarded_client`, an httpx client whose request hook runs `private_address_refusal` on every hop including redirects, refusing non-http(s) URLs, localhost, single-label hosts and any literal or DNS-resolved address that is not public (covering inet_aton forms, IPv4-mapped, 6to4, Teredo and NAT64); a check that cannot decide refuses. It is used directly by `download_file`, the robots.txt fetch and the grant-calls pull, while Import's `read_page` and `search_public_sources` go through `check_url`, which calls the same address check, and `web.py` itself only builds the Tavily search tool.

TAVILY_API_KEY is optional: without it Import's `search_public_sources` returns a SEARCH UNAVAILABLE message instead of failing, and the news collector posts advanced news searches to api.tavily.com with three attempts, raising SearchFailed so the watermark does not advance.

Langfuse tracing is enabled only when both public and secret keys are set; configure_langfuse falls back to VERCEL_ENV and VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA for environment and release, attaches a payload mask when building the client, verifies credentials via auth_check (disabling tracing with an error if rejected), never takes the app down on failure, and runs lazily when agents are first built (before build_agent) rather than at process boot; traces are flushed after each agent run because serverless functions freeze after responding, with a best-effort client shutdown at lifespan teardown.

The Graphiti/Neo4j knowledge graph is optional and activates only when both NEO4J_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY are set (Neo4j Aura when deployed, a bundled container locally); graphiti_core is imported lazily and a disabled graph logs a reason so the app still boots.

The Deploy workflow is workflow_dispatch-only and serialises runs per ref with a concurrency group and cancel-in-progress false, so a production deploy in flight is queued behind rather than cancelled; nothing deploys automatically because Git deployment is disabled in both vercel.json files.

ci.yml runs on every pull request and every push to master, deploys nothing, uses a per-ref concurrency group that cancels in-progress runs, and has four jobs: backend-lint (ruff), backend-unit, backend-integration and frontend (npm ci, lint, tsc --noEmit, coverage with Codecov upload, build).

The backend-integration CI job runs against a pgvector/pgvector:pg17 service on port 5433, applies db/init/*.sql, the migration runner and the seeders, runs pytest -m integration with skips listed, and deselects two migration-integrity tests that need a restore of the original dump.

The Dependency review workflow runs actions/dependency-review-action@v4 on pull requests with fail-on-severity high and comments in the PR only on failure; it checks only what the PR's lockfile changes add, while already-open advisories stay in Dependabot alerts.

The two backend CI test jobs and the frontend job upload coverage to Codecov (flags backend+backend-unit, backend+backend-integration, frontend) using GitHub OIDC (tokenless fallback for fork PRs); codecov.yml carries flags forward, turns the global project/patch statuses off and gates the backend and frontend components separately, each with a 75% floor project check, a project check that may not fall more than 1% below base, and a 75% patch check, with `fixes` rules mapping report paths to backend/ and frontend/ directories.

Dependabot-driven version bumps (next 16.3.8, CopilotKit ~1.75.2, undici/katex npm overrides, PyJWT 2.15.1) are recorded in the changelog and package manifests, and there is no .github/dependabot.yml in the repository; such bumps reach production only through the hand-run Deploy workflow.
Only deploy.yml deploys to Vercel and only via workflow_dispatch; CI, Dependency review and Codecov are checks only.

Outbound TLS trust is owned by egress.py: `TRUST` is an SSL context of certifi's roots plus extra intermediates from `app/core/certs/intermediates.pem` (currently emSign SSL CA - G1, which censusindia.gov.in fails to send), with verification and hostname checking still on; both `guarded_client` and Import's research reader client use it, and tests pin that each bundled cert is an in-date intermediate whose root is already trusted.

`open_checkpointer` runs no DDL: it reads `checkpoint_migrations`, compares with `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` (the last migration the installed langgraph expects) and raises a RuntimeError telling the operator to run `make migrate` if the tables are missing or at another version, so a backend will not start against an unmigrated or out-of-date checkpoint schema.
